# kenji

44, Osaka. Calibration technician in a metrology lab - he spends his working
day establishing what an instrument's reading is worth, and he brought the
habit home.

Twenty-five weeks of record in two deliberate blocks: twelve at a modest
deficit, thirteen at maintenance. He weighs every morning on the same bench
scale, before eating, after voiding, and he weighs his food.

## Why he exists

Every other weight series in this corpus is a path the generator walked - a
start and a step, with the step small enough to look like progress. Four of
them move by a gram or two a day and never reverse, which is a body that does
not fluctuate (#459). And the demo takes weight from one random stream and its
two energy figures from two others, so the correlation between a deficit and a
weight change is zero by construction (#458).

His record is built the other way round. His weight is not drawn at all: each
morning's mass is carried forward from the balance he logged that day, and
only the READING is drawn, at a scatter taken from published single-subject
work rather than chosen.

## What he disagrees with

He thinks a number without an interval is not a result. The engine answers a
weekly rate with a DIRECTION - `losing`, `on_target` - and to him a direction
word where an interval belongs is a category error rather than a
simplification. He would rather it printed nothing.

His second block exists to ask a question the engine has no verb for: not "am
I losing" but "how many more mornings must I weigh before a slope this small
separates from zero". He writes the count down every Sunday, because there is
nowhere in the schema to put it.
